purpose: keep every certificate valid, inventoried and renewed on time, so no outage is caused by an expiry
entry_criteria: TLS is in use on several endpoints (stage 135)
A certificate inventory source exists or can be built
procedure: Discover certificates from the authorities, load balancers, clusters and by scanning your address ranges, and record issuer, names, expiry, owner and where installed.
Automate renewal wherever possible, and track the exceptions that need manual steps with an owner and a calendar date.
Monitor expiry from outside, and alert at several stages (for example 30, 14 and 7 days) to different recipients with escalation.
Check the renewal result by confirming the new certificate is served, not only that issuance succeeded.
Revoke and replace when a key is exposed or a name is retired, and remove retired certificates from the inventory.
Practise the emergency replacement of an expired certificate and record the time it takes.
acceptance_criteria: Every certificate has an owner and an expiry date in the inventory
Alerts run at several stages with escalation
Renewal is verified by what is served

validation.command: echo | openssl s_client -connect app.example.com:443 -servername app.example.com 2>/dev/null | openssl x509 -noout -enddate   # example
validation.expect: expiry is later than the alert threshold

validation.check: compare the inventory with a scan of the address ranges
validation.expect: no certificate found that is not in the inventory

failure_modes.response: Replace now and add the alert

failure_modes.mode: Renewal succeeded but old certificate is served
failure_modes.response: Reload the service and add a verification step

failure_modes.detection: Scan finds one not in inventory
failure_modes.response: Find owner and register or remove

worked_example: ILLUSTRATIVE: A weekly scan finds a certificate on a forgotten admin host with 19 days left; the owner is identified, it is moved to automated issuance, and a monitor now alerts at 30, 14 and 7 days.
